2026 Holiday gift guide for woodworkers
November 24, 2026 | 10:47 am CST
The Lie-Nielsen bronze low-angle block plane is woodworking bling that actually works, and it makes a great gift.

Most woodworkers are pragmatic and practical. They like gifts they can really use. We’ve compiled a list for 2026 that spans most price ranges and goes from useful bling to essential safety accessories to just plain fun.
Speaking planes, the first item on our list might be considered woodworking jewelry, but besides being gorgeous, it’s really useful. Let’s get started.

Lie Nielsen No. 102 Low Angle Block Plane
Based on the Stanley No. 102, this small plane fits perfectly in the hand, slips easily into the pocket, and is destined to become the most useful tool in your workshop. The low-angle blade is 1/8-inch thick for chatter-free cuts and the unobtrusive stainless steel adjuster offers blade control of micrometer ease and precision with minimum backlash. The bronze body makes it stand out from all the cast iron stuff in the shop. My staff gave me an engraved one of these when I left Fine Woodworking magazine, and it doesn’t just sit on the shelf looking pretty. I’ve used it almost daily for more than 25 years. $160. Made in Maine by Lie-Nielsen Toolworks.

ISOtunes FREE 2.0 earbuds
A true wireless earbud hearing protector with a 25 dB noise reduction rating plus Bluetooth 5.2 technology, the ISOtunes FREE 2.0 provides enhanced noise reduction and functionality for an enhanced audio experience with a comfortable cordless fit. Listen to your tunes, answer your phone, and protect your ears from loud machinery in the shop. $129.99.

FastCap Pro Carpenter tape measures
The FastCap ProCarpenter Auto Lock tape measure combines all the innovative features of the original ProCarpenter with a convenient auto-lock mechanism. Pull the blade out and it stays exactly where you want it until you press the release button. Other features that make this a shop favorite include an erasable panel you can write on with a pencil, a pencil sharpener, and an easy-to-use belt clip. $14.58. I have a whole bunch of these in my shop strategically located just about everywhere so I don’t have to look far for a tape measure.

Work clothing that actually works
Tired of jeans that wear out in the knees way too fast? And speaking of knees, how about something that painlessly protects them? For decades I’ve been a big fan of European-style work pants with built-in knee pad and nail pouch pockets. I go back and forth with two major brands, the Swedish Blaklader brand and the Norwegian Helly Hansen brand.

They are both great. I think the Blakladers are a little tougher and last longer, but the Helly Hansen versions are more comfortable, have better knee pads, and easier access to change the pads. You can’t go wrong with either, but be warned they are not cheap, and don’t forget to order the knee pads when you order the pants, as they are extra. The pants come in various models but expect to pay north of $100 and another $30+ for the pads. Still worth it.

Dust collection accessories
Dust collection is not just a convenience. It improves safety and the quality of your work. Here are a couple of low-cost, high value items from Oneida Air Systems and Rockler to help woodworkers improve their dust collection.

The dust-free router hood from Oneida Air Systems is used on portable fixed-base and plunge routers. The hood collects router waste from both above and below the bit, virtually eliminating post-project cleanup, facilitating fine detail work, and reducing wear and tear on bits, the company says. The hood is molded from clear polycarbonate for high visibility and fits most portable fixed-base or plunge routers. $34.95.

Power Tool Hose Kit
I don’t know about you, but I’m often frustrated connecting portable power tools to shop vacuums. It seems like the hoses never match up. Rockler offers the Dust Right FlexiPort power tool hose kit, offering all the features of their well-loved FlexiPort system, plus the Click-Connect feature for fast, easy switching of a single hose between multiple tools. The kit includes four FlexiPorts of varying diameters, plus the Click-Connect Hose Adapter, which threads into the included Expandable Hose. Three of the four FlexiPorts have a clasp that you can ratchet down for a secure connection to the tool. Finally, a vent collar lets you adjust the suction level—perfect for reducing swirl marks when orbital sanding. Regularly $49.99, it’s currently on sale at $24.99.

Logo branding kit
Nothing says craftsmanship like a logo branded into your work. There are lots of options for logo brands, ranging from inexpensive irons you heat with a torch to handier electric units in a wide range of wattages. They are available from lots of different outlets but this Etsy store seems offer most of the options, including custom logos, all in one place. Prices range from the low double digits to several hundred dollars, and remember custom orders take some time, so order early for gift giving.

Give the gift of lean organization
Kaizen Foam from FastCap turns messy tool drawers and walls into clean, professional shadow boards. Simply trace, cut, and peel — every tool has its own perfect custom-fit home. Instantly see what's missing and stay organized. Kits come in a wide range of thicknesses and sizes starting at $43.99.

Take notes or sketch in style
Capture your thoughts or sketch your designs like a boss with a Calavera Shop Journal. Built from the same hard-wearing leather used across the company’s apron line, these bound journals will last forever, looking better with use. Available in a variety of sizes and colors, each journal features a pair of removable inserts. Once filled, simply pull them out and replace them with a couple of spares, available right here. (seriously, you're going to fill this thing up, so don't forget the spares). Prices range from $25 to $40.

Humorous gifts
When I was editor of Fine Woodworking magazine, the magazine’s founder, Paul Roman, told me to avoid humor in the publication because, “Woodworkers don’t have a sense of humor.” Of course, we all know that is wrong, although humor is indeed in the eye of the beholder. If the woodworker you are shopping for likes a laugh, there are plenty of silly items designed to earn a smile or a chuckle, including T-shirts, mugs, and even carpenter’s pencils with pithy sayings. Etsy is a good place to look for these items. Some of the lines that made me smile include:
• Measure Once, Cuss Twice (or Measure Twice, Cuss Once)
• Woodworking, Because Murder is Wrong
• Rock, Paper, Scissors, Table Saw (with graphic depiction of missing digits for the last one)
• Jig [jig] (noun) A thing you build to build the thing.
Have something to say? Share your thoughts with us in the comments below.

William Sampson is a lifelong woodworker, and he has been an advocate for small-scale entrepreneurs and lean manufacturing since the 1980s. He was the editor of Fine Woodworking magazine in the early 1990s and founded WoodshopBusiness magazine, which he eventually sold and merged with CabinetMaker magazine. He helped found the Cabinet Makers Association in 1998 and was its first executive director. Today, as editorial director of Woodworking Network and FDMC magazine he has more than 20 years experience covering the professional woodworking industry. His popular "In the Shop" tool reviews and videos appear monthly in FDMC.
